documents.content:
Reduced-fare transit pass

Residents aged sixty-five or older and riders with a certified disability may apply for a reduced-fare pass. Applications require proof of identity and eligibility. Approved cards are mailed within ten business days.

Accessible transit booking

Door-to-door accessible rides must be booked by 5 p.m. on the day before travel. Same-day requests are accepted only when capacity remains. A companion travels without charge when the rider's eligibility record requires assistance.

Residential parking permits

A household may receive two resident permits and one visitor permit. Applicants provide vehicle registration and proof of address. Visitor permits expire at the end of the calendar year and cannot be transferred to another address.

Temporary street closures

Applications for a block event must be filed at least thirty days in advance. The organizer supplies a traffic plan and proof of insurance. Emergency vehicle access must remain open throughout the event.

Curbside recycling

Paper, metal cans and rigid plastic containers belong in the blue cart. Plastic bags, batteries and food waste are prohibited. Collection occurs every other Wednesday, and items must be loose rather than bagged.

Bulky item collection

Households may schedule two free bulky-item pickups each calendar year. Each pickup is limited to four items. Construction debris, tires and hazardous chemicals are not accepted through this service.

Water leak response

A leak before the property meter is repaired by the city. A leak after the meter is the owner's responsibility. Suspected main breaks causing flooding or loss of pressure should be reported to the emergency line immediately.

Water billing disputes

Customers must dispute a meter reading within sixty days of the bill date. The utility reviews meter history and may perform an inspection. Payment of the undisputed portion remains due while the review is open.

Public tree service

The city prunes trees located between the sidewalk and curb on a five-year cycle. Residents need a permit before removing a public tree. Private-yard trees are maintained by the property owner unless they create an immediate public hazard.

Noise complaints

Construction noise is allowed from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays. Non-emergency complaints are filed online. Active threats or violence should be reported to emergency services.

Pet licensing

Dogs and cats older than four months require an annual license and current rabies vaccination. A discounted license is available for sterilized animals. A veterinarian letter is required for a medical vaccination exemption.

Mobile food vendors

A mobile food unit needs a health permit and a separate location permit. Food-safety inspection must be completed before sales begin. Vendors may not operate within one hundred feet of a school entrance during school hours.

Building inspections

Electrical and plumbing work must remain visible until the required inspection passes. Inspection requests submitted before 3 p.m. are normally scheduled for the next business day. Inspectors do not approve design changes in the field.

Public records requests

Requests should identify the records and a date range; a reason is not required. The records office acknowledges requests within five business days. Fees may cover duplication but not the time spent locating records.

Emergency shelter activation

Warming shelters open when the forecast is fifteen degrees Fahrenheit or below for four consecutive hours. Cooling shelters open when the heat index is forecast to reach one hundred degrees. Service animals are admitted at every shelter.

Snow emergency parking

During a declared snow emergency, vehicles must leave marked snow routes within two hours. Towing begins after that window. The declaration remains active until the transportation department publishes an official cancellation.
